ENGINE TRIGGER LAB

REPLAY RECENT VISUALS

Breath, bolts and bursts play once. Clouds, walls and wards linger. Real melee attacks show their resolved hit, miss or critical. Replays repeat no rolls or damage.

Visual tests only. The Rust engine fixes the origin and aim; a following ward stays attached to its token. No attack roll, damage, healing, save, spell resource or teleport movement is resolved by these test triggers. Transport uses a ghost copy of the source art at the selected destination.

What these previews do

Boundaries show geometry, not adjudicated targets. Effects do not yet clip to walls or decide which squares are affected. Ranged trajectories and melee markers are illustrations, not reach or hit validation.

THE BESTIARY CABINET

Faces in the dark

306 approved creatures. The Rust registry owns each asset, its footprint and integrity hash. Assigning artwork changes appearance only; its footprint must match the selected actor.

Controls: drag tokens normally, or right-click while dragging to pin waypoints. Arrow keys / WASD still work; Q/E/Z/C move diagonally (alternating 5/10 ft across the turn, including Dash). Ctrl+Z undoes the whole move until another action. Measure draws a temporary geometric ruler; right-click adds bends, Escape clears.

About this playtest

A real Rust engine compiled to WebAssembly resolves this local encounter. No Fantasy Grounds, Lua, Python or model server is needed to play the hosted version.

Effects atelier adds visual templates with movable, fixed and token-attached placement. These graphics do not resolve spell mechanics, damage, affected squares or wall clipping. The Engine trigger lab is a visual demonstration.

Implemented: seeded initiative and dice; straight movement, alternating 5/10-foot diagonals and movement budgets; occupied spaces and axis-aligned walls; gates; melee attacks and critical hits; Dash; simplified Dodge; turn advancement; HP; defeated-token skipping; save/load; and a Rust-owned registry of all 306 token PNGs.

Characters: use Characters to import XML, text/form PDFs, Google Sheets CSV or pasted cells, review the sheet, or create a level 1 SRD foundation. Only the basic combat profile is projected into the table; spells and features remain sheet data.

Not yet a full D&D engine: the default actors are synthetic training profiles. No opportunity attacks, reactions, spells, bonus actions, class features, death saves, cover, lighting, fog, environmental effects or multiplayer. Defeated tokens simply leave the training fight. Door interaction is free in this prototype. Dodge assumes all combatants see one another. These limitations are not new adventure rules.

This is a local GM/hotseat session. The browser holds all state; it is not a trusted multiplayer server. Saves are editable local files, not authenticated campaign records.

Your progress is kept in this browser. Save downloads a portable JSON session; Load asks the Rust engine to validate it. Export downloads the resolved message record, with an additional map-update field for gate changes.

Performance: Mythastria runs on your own computer. The 3D view uses your graphics card, and the simulator (Play live, Simulator fights, and Remix’s proof fights) uses your processor, so on an older or slower PC they can be slow. The full release will list recommended minimum system requirements for reasonable performance.

GM tip (Remix): encounter tests are most accurate with your own group’s characters. Ask each player before keeping a copy of their sheet for test fights. Remix (coming) will keep only the game numbers (no backstory, portrait or real name), on your computer only, and delete a copy whenever a player asks.
